note: No publication process exists for a built render-worker image. The repository's only image process is an image-INPUT fingerprint (data/rcap-staging-action.json, generated by scripts/generate-rcap-staging-action.mjs and checked by scripts/verify-rcap-image-input-fingerprint.mjs). It records the hashes of the paths the Dockerfile copies; it does not record a built image, and there is no push, registry or digest-publication step anywhere in scripts/ or docs/. This file therefore records the local build, and nothing here claims a published or deployable image.

image.digestScope: Local content digest from the containerd snapshotter. It is NOT a registry digest: the image was not pushed, so no registry digest exists and none may be recorded on an artifact as container_digest.

reproducibility.note: Rebuilding the same committed tree produced a different top-level manifest digest (sha256:3a0357d880d62301b859244f2c8bdec743d1d8c58f428cce4bb50bf83c830e22) while every one of the 23 rootfs layers was byte-identical. BuildKit stamps an attestation manifest with build metadata, so the manifest digest is not reproducible; the filesystem content is. Identify this image by the rootfs layer set above, not by the manifest digest alone.

baseImage.obtainedVia: docker pull mirror.gcr.io/library/node:22-slim, retagged locally to node:22-slim. Docker Hub's own blob CDN (production.cloudfront.docker.com) is denied by this session's egress policy with a gateway 403, so the Hub pull cannot complete; mirror.gcr.io serves the identical library image and is reachable. The Dockerfile still says FROM node:22-slim and was not changed for this.

smokeTests.command: docker run --rm --network none rcap-render-worker:del-d node deploy/rcap-render-worker/preflight.mjs
smokeTests.proved: All 67 packaged files present and byte-identical to the manifest; the worker's module graph loaded inside the image (which requires the @/../data ESM JSON imports); 51 compiled jurisdiction profiles resolved; the Grade-A authority gate returned a reasoned decision for all 14 registry records - 2 ALLOWED (DC:dc_actual_innocence_expungement_16_803, WY:felony-conviction-expungement-w-s-7-13-1502) and 12 reasoned refusals - identical to the same code run from the source checkout.

smokeTests.command: docker run --rm --network none rcap-render-worker:del-d node scripts/rcap-render-worker.mjs --once
smokeTests.proved: The real worker entry point loads its whole module graph from the packaged layout and reaches its first real decision, refusing for the right reason: 'rcap-render-worker: Supabase is not configured; the worker has no storage or queue to run against.' No database was configured, so this is the correct refusal rather than a data defect.

smokeTests.command: docker run --rm --network none -v /tmp/empty-specs:/app/data/record-clearing/packet-specifications:ro rcap-render-worker:del-d node deploy/rcap-render-worker/preflight.mjs
smokeTests.proved: Hiding the packaged specification directory makes the preflight report 19 missing files and fail. The packaged data is load-bearing, not decorative.

smokeTests.command: docker run --rm --network none -v /tmp/empty-ledger:/app/data/rcap-ledger:ro rcap-render-worker:del-d node scripts/rcap-render-worker.mjs --once
smokeTests.proved: Without the packaged data/rcap-ledger files the worker dies at module load with ENOENT on data/rcap-ledger/packet-correction-required.json. This is exactly the state every image built from the previous Dockerfile was in, because it copied no data/ at all.

publication.statement: The image was not pushed to any registry. No prior image may be claimed to contain this packaging: the fulfillment registry pins provider.imageDigest sha256:bf4589d3432f396f08196b2a619e445b75f1b4e2d2a0c404fbb06c4017e61864 on its records, and that digest predates the data layers added here.
